key_insight: A dilated causal CNN can detect radiation-induced charge jumps in superconducting qubits fast enough for real-time control, not just offline analysis.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables FPGA-deployable, in-the-loop charge-jump detection on QICK, supporting adaptive qubit control and potentially improving error mitigation in quantum processors.
method: Train a DCCNN on synthetic Ramsey tomography scans built from measured qubit templates.
Translate the model to FPGA firmware with hls4ml using ap_fixed<16,6> quantization.
Deploy on Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC hardware to achieve 6.19 µs per inference.
evidence_signal: At matched false-positive rate on |Δq| ∈ [0.1, 0.5] e, the DCCNN reached 0.843 ± 0.022 detection efficiency versus 0.866 ± 0.020 for the offline χ² baseline.
watch_item: Performance is shown on synthetic data derived from measured templates, so robustness to broader device drift and unseen operating conditions still needs validation.
paper_title: Real-Time Detection of Charge Jumps in Superconducting Qubits with a Convolutional Neural Network
